prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the passenger in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1169; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd prefer to just go by the claimant for this, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were sitting in the vehicle at the time of the collision?

A: I was in the front passenger seat. The driver was taking us along the main road toward the shopping center when the car ahead slowed down pretty suddenly.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I was looking at my phone, so I only noticed when we jolted forward. There was a loud bang and my head snapped back and then forward.

Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?

A: Yes, I had it on the whole time.

Q: Did you feel any pain right after the collision?

A: My neck hurt almost immediately, and by the next morning it was stiff and sore. Turning my head to the left is the worst. I also got a dull headache that lasted a couple of days.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening. They checked my range of motion, told me it looked like a neck strain, and gave me a prescription for a muscle relaxer and some anti-inflammatories.

Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since then?

A: I've been going to a physical therapist twice a week. My doctor wants me to keep that up for a few more weeks and see how things improve.

Q: Has the pain affected your daily activities or work?

A: It has. I had to take some time off from lifting at work, and sleeping has been uncomfortable because of the stiffness.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm still hopeful I'll get back to normal soon. Thank you for listening.
